title: Polymer‐Directed Crystal Growth Regulation: Template‐Free Synthesis of Mesoporous Single‐Crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3
abstract: ABSTRACT Transition metal borates are attractive anode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) because of their high specific capacity and environmental benignity; however, their structural collapse induced by large volume changes during cycling leads to rapid capacity degradation. In this study, we report a polymer‐directed crystal growth regulation strategy that enables the template‐free synthesis of mesoporous single‐crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3 (MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 ). Polyethyleneimine (PEI) acts as a bifunctional regulator, coordinating Mn 2+ ions and hydrogen bonding with borate ions to modulate hydrolysis and condensation, thereby yielding a hybrid precursor. Subsequent hydrothermal treatment yields single‐crystalline MnBO 2 OH nanobelts, which are converted by calcination into MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 . As an anode active material for lithium‐ion batteries, MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 delivers a reversible capacity of 1440 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 , more than twice that of bulk Mn 2 OBO 3 . Notably, this polymer‐directed strategy is readily extendable to doped MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 (e.g., Fe, V, and Mg), providing a versatile platform for the design of porous single‐crystalline materials for energy storage.

title: Preparation and Electrochemical Performance Study of Covalent Organic Framework-Derived Porous Carbon@FeS2
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer designable skeletons and ordered pore domains, but poor charge transport and insufficient electrochemically active sites hinder their direct use as electrodes. In this work, COF-Bq was first obtained by Knoevenagel condensation and then transformed by carbonization and KOH activation into COF-BqC-700-3. A hydrothermal step grew FeS₂ within and on this porous carbon, giving COF-BqC-700-3@FeS₂ composites. The optimized COF-BqC-700-3@FeS₂-160-2 maintained hierarchical porosity dominated by micropores and reached 740.2 F g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹. When assembled with COF-BqC-700-3 in an asymmetric device, it delivered 25.03 Wh kg⁻¹ at 750 W kg⁻¹. The device retained 90.95% capacitance after 5,000 cycles and showed 99.93% Coulombic efficiency. These results show that FeS₂ adds Faradaic storage sites to COF-derived carbon while the porous carbon framework supports charge transfer and ion transport.

title: Bioinspired Buffered Microenvironment Enables Highly Crystalline 3D COF Gels With Controllable Structures for Exceptional Molecular Adsorption
abstract: ABSTRACT Reconciling long‐range crystallinity with macroscopic network formation remains a central challenge in constructing three‐dimensional covalent organic framework (3D COF) gels. Inspired by biomineralization and tofu coagulation, we propose a synergistic buffered system with salt bridges for direct assembly of crystalline 3D COF gels via imine condensation. Ten metal salts were selected to regulate stable and buffered pH microenvironment. Comparing various salts revealed a correlation between pH microenvironment and the formation state and crystallinity of COFs. NaAc emerges as representative regulator for multiple roles: (i) forming AcO − /AcOH buffer to maintain a stable weakly acidic microenvironment and promote disorder‐to‐order transition, (ii) regulating kinetics, defect healing, and COF topology, and (iii) Na + as salt bridges stabilizing the 3D gel network. Pore topology can be switched between two crystalline phases by varying side substituents and salt addition sequence, as seen by XRD peak shift from 8.9° to 6.6°. The gels have low density (0.028–0.042 g/cm 3 ), high compressive strength, CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 140, organic solvent uptake up to 80 times their weight, and over 90% capacity retention after 20 cycles. Overall, this work establishes a paradigm from microenvironment engineering and ion selection to topology regulation and adsorption, providing a blueprint for functional 3D COF gels.

title: Promoting photocatalytic methane oxidative coupling via gradient oxidation field engineering
abstract: Abstract The efficient and selective photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) into valuable chemicals remains an unresolved challenge in modern science. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of a robust photocatalyst by constructing photocatalytic gradient oxidation field on mesoporous TiO2, which demonstrates exceptional OCM performance and outperforms other benchmark photocatalysts. The optimized photocatalytic system exhibits a high CH4 conversion rate of 1.2 mmol h−1, a high C2 hydrocarbon space-time yield of 82.7 mmol g−1 h−1 and 90.1% C2 selectivity, accompanied by a remarkable apparent quantum efficiency of over 11.6%. Mechanism analyses reveal that the gradient oxidation field introduced by the Au nanoislands and Pd atomic satellites can optimize the oxidation activity and selectivity with hydroxide and superoxide radicals, respectively. The synergistic interaction between the Au and Pd sites facilitates favorable adsorption of O2/CH4 reactants and promotes fast desorption of the C2H6 product, thereby accelerating the overall OCM process. This work demonstrates the critical role of photocatalytic oxidation field, and opens a new avenue for developing efficient and selective catalysts for various photocatalytic applications.

title: Guest‐Directed Navigation of a Ligand Conformational Landscape Enables Palladium‐Organic Cage–Bowl–Helicate Interconversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Biological systems regulate molecular function by reshaping conformational energy landscapes in response to external stimuli. Translating this principle into artificial supramolecular systems remains challenging, particularly when multiple structurally distinct states must be accessed using a single class of stimulus. Here, we report a conformationally adaptive ligand L comprising two 2,4,6‐tris(4‐pyridyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TPT) panels connected by a conformationally flexible 3,3′‐disubstituted biphenyl spacer. Coordination of L with (en)Pd(II) affords a discrete Pd 4 L 2 cage 1 . Distinct guests redirect the assembly landscape along divergent pathways: 6‐methylcoumarin ( G1 ) induces the bowl‐shaped Pd 4 L 2 complex ( G1 ) 4 ⊂ 2 , whereas 1‐adamantanol ( G2 ) selects the Pd 6 L 3 triple‐stranded helicate ( G2 ) 8 ⊂ 3 . Cage 1 , bowl 2 , and helicate 3 correspond to trans‐/cis‐, cis‐/cis‐, and cis‐/trans‐ combinations of the biphenyl spacer and TPT‐panel orientations, respectively. Guest‐exchange experiments reveal path‐dependent interconversion: G1 converts helicate 3 toward a mixture of cage 1 and bowl 2 , whereas guest removal restores cage 1 , enabling G2 to redirect it back to helicate 3 . Thus, the system can be precisely navigated among cage, bowl, and helicate architectures solely through guest addition, removal, and exchange. A 4,4′‐biphenyl‐linked analogue shows no comparable conversion. These results establish a guest‐addressable three‐state self‐assembly landscape in which distinct combinations of ligand cis‐/trans‐ conformations encode divergent supramolecular architectures.

title: Processing-induced self-organised triboelectric interfaces enable event-responsive cementitious composites
abstract: Structural materials are commonly designed to bear loads passively, whereas sensing and energy-harvesting functions are typically implemented using externally attached devices that are vulnerable to damage and interfacial failure. Here we report a processing-induced strategy for forming self-organised triboelectric interfaces directly within fibre-reinforced cementitious composites during vibration-assisted casting. Through fresh-state flow, fibre migration, and grid-assisted interception, conductive and dielectric constituents assemble into local fibre-enriched contact regions, enabling intrinsic electromechanical transduction without post-fabrication assembly. Microstructural characterisation reveals local fibre enrichment and fibre-grid interweaving around the embedded coated grid, while first-principles calculations support the interfacial charge redistribution between polyvinyl alcohol and polytetrafluoroethylene. The composites retain high mechanical toughness while exhibiting stable electrical responses under low-frequency mechanical excitation, with signal amplitude scaling with load and contact configuration. After cracking, newly created internal interfaces continue to provide functional output, demonstrating damage-tolerant electromechanical activity. We further demonstrate an event-triggered sensing system in which the embedded interfaces serve as self-powered signal sources for wake-up and alert operations. This work establishes a processing-driven route for programming functional interfaces within structural materials and provides a basis for intrinsically responsive infrastructure components. The study shows that vibration-assisted casting forms fibre-polymer contacts inside a cementitious composite, enabling electrical signals after damage and a laboratory demonstration of event-triggered alerts.

title: Scalable Hydrogel‐Programmed Porous Photonic Cement for Passive Daytime Cooling
abstract: ABSTRACT Cement is among the most widely produced materials on Earth, yet its strong solar absorption causes building envelopes to act as heat sources, increasing cooling energy demand. Here, we structurally program cement hydration to transform conventional cementitious materials into passive cooling interfaces. Through hydrogel‐confined mineralization of cement clinker, we construct a robust, hierarchically porous calcium–silicate–hydrate (C–S–H) network that integrates broadband light scattering, vapor transport and thermal insulation. By regulating the composition and crystallinity of the hydrates, the material achieves ∼95% solar reflectance and ∼98% infrared emissivity without the use of additional photonic fillers. The hygroscopic nature of the network further enables sustained evaporative cooling under humid or cloudy conditions where radiative cooling alone becomes inefficient. Life‐cycle analysis indicates that this strategy provides a pathway to transform high‐emission cement into carbon‐mitigating materials integrated within opaque building envelopes, enabling the scalable deployment of daytime radiative cooling across the built environment.

title: Hydroxyl‐Rich Sodium Gluconate Enables Dense SAM Assembly and Enhances Conductivity in NiO x ‐Based Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Nickel oxide (NiO x )/self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) composite hole transport layers represent a promising configuration for inverted perovskite solar cells (IPSCs). Nevertheless, the insufficient electrical conductivity of NiO x and the limited number of binding sites on its surface lead to incomplete monolayer coverage, resulting in substantial interfacial charge losses that constrain efficiency improvements. To address these issues, we introduce hydroxyl‑rich sodium gluconate (SG) into the NiO x solution. Gluconate anions from SG modulate the electronic properties of NiO x , thereby enhancing its conductivity. Meanwhile, the abundant hydroxyl groups along the SG backbone furnish additional hydrogen‐bonding sites for the subsequent adsorption of the SAM, promoting the formation of a compact and well‐ordered interfacial molecular layer. This dense SAM not only suppresses leakage currents but also optimizes the energetic cascade at the heterojunction, ultimately enabling the resulting IPSCs to achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.24%. During maximum‐power‐point operation under ISOS‑L‑1 protocol, the optimized device preserves 91.6% of the starting output after 1000 h. This work establishes a versatile interfacial engineering approach that overcomes limitations in both SAM assembly and charge transport, offering new opportunities for the development of highly efficient and durable IPSCs.

title: Electron-Catalyzed Supramolecular Assembly with High Efficiency, Robustness, and Versatility
abstract: Abstract Although catalysis is widely exploited by nature to orchestrate noncovalent supramolecular assembly and build up complex living systems, its utilization in synthetic chemistry has conventionally been limited to accelerating covalent reactions. Consequently, the development of artificial systems for catalytic assembly remains a formidable and largely unexplored challenge. Here, we present a rationally designed strategy of electron-catalyzed supramolecular assembly, wherein the electron acts as an efficient, robust, and versatile catalyst to accelerate the formation of a donor–acceptor complex. Optimization of the elementary steps and intermediate stability yields an efficient catalytic cycle, furnishing the process with both a high turnover number and operational robustness in open air. Furthermore, the electron catalysis can be readily triggered by diverse external stimuli─including electricity, light, and mechanical force─enabling precise spatiotemporal control over the assembly process and near-quantitative synthesis of supramolecular complexes. Collectively, this work establishes a well-elucidated strategy of catalytic assembly with remarkable practicality, advancing the frontiers of noncovalent synthetic chemistry.

title: Identification of the Intrinsic Ordering Effect of PtCo Intermetallic Catalysts on Fuel Cell Durability
abstract: ABSTRACT The dissolution of 3d transition metals is a central bottleneck limiting the practical use of Pt‐alloy cathode catalysts in fuel cells. Although ordered intermetallic compounds (IMCs) have been explored for nearly 4 decades as a route to mitigate this instability, the durability benefit of structural ordering itself remains debated and has rarely been reliably validated under practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) conditions. Herein, we design a phase‐diagram‐guided sequential annealing protocol that yields an ordered/disordered PtCo catalyst pair with closely matched particle size and composition, enabling the durability effect of structural ordering to be rigorously isolated. In practical MEAs, structural ordering does not translate into a significant H 2 ‐air performance gain but markedly slows catalyst degradation. For example, after 90 000 cycles of accelerated durability test, the ordered catalyst loses only 28 mV at 1.5 A cm −2 , less than half that of its disordered counterpart (65 mV). Correlative in situ MEA diagnostics, electron microscopy, and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry trace this enhanced durability to suppressed Co outward diffusion and dissolution. Machine‐learning‐accelerated theoretical calculations further rationalize this stabilization by revealing a higher thermodynamic penalty for Co surface segregation and a larger kinetic barrier for Co diffusion toward neighboring vacancies in the ordered IMC.

title: Concise and Modular Access to a Chiral Biaryl Monophosphine Library and Downstream Use in Catalytic Enantioselective Transformations
abstract: ABSTRACT Atropoisomeric biaryl monophosphines, chiral variants of Buchwald‐type ligands, are powerful ligands for asymmetric catalysis. However, their synthesis relies heavily on resolution or step‐intensive synthetic approaches, restricting structural diversity and tuning options, thus limiting systematic exploration of their catalytic potential. We report a unified strategy for streamlined access to a broadly tunable family of atrop‐chiral biaryl monophosphines. The three‐step assembly protocol first exploits a Cp X ‐Ir III ‐catalyzed atroposelective C─H arylation of phosphine oxide to forge the biaryl core with three different diversity points. Subsequently, reduction to the phosphine and installation of the fourth diversity point provide a diverse library of 35 chiral air‐stable monophosphine ligands. Their catalytic performance was benchmarked in a challenging enantioselective gold‐catalyzed cycloisomerization and a palladium‐catalyzed asymmetric phenol dearomatization, leading to the discovery of high‐performing library members providing excellent enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er in both transformations.

title: Stimuli-responsive mesoporous silica nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems
abstract: Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) are versatile inorganic nanocarriers whose ordered mesopores, high surface area, tunable pore dimensions, and modifiable surfaces permit loading and controlled release of diverse therapeutic cargos. This review evaluates stimuli-responsive MSN design through an explicit evidence-grading lens: each proposed trigger is considered in relation to the primary study, biological model, demonstrated response, and principal limitation. Endogenous cues include pH, glutathione/redox conditions, reactive oxygen species, enzymes, glucose, ATP, and hypoxia; exogenous triggers include temperature, light, magnetic fields, and ultrasound. These cues can be coupled to molecular gates, cleavable linkers, responsive polymers, charge-reversal systems, or hybrid components. The review considers MSN architectures, synthesis and template removal, surface functionalization, drug loading and release, characterization, biological evaluation, and biomedical applications. Particular attention is paid to the distinction between chemical responsiveness and biological selectivity, and between in vitro , ex vivo , animal, and clinical evidence. Translational constraints include protein-corona formation, biological heterogeneity, biodistribution, intracellular trafficking, residual template or surfactant, sterilization, batch reproducibility, scale-up, and regulatory complexity. Emerging biodegradable and biomimetic MSNs, nucleic-acid delivery, theranostics, precision nanomedicine, and data-assisted formulation development are treated as developing rather than uniformly established technologies. The review’s contribution is a comparative framework for asking whether each added responsive function produces a measurable benefit over a simpler carrier, rather than assuming that greater structural complexity improves therapeutic performance. The evidence-based framework used here distinguishes the level of testing from the strength of the claim: in vitro release or cell data establish proof of concept, ex vivo data address selected tissue-level behavior, animal studies provide preclinical evidence, and clinical evidence requires human evaluation of the specific responsive MSN system. Clinical experience with other silica-containing materials is not equivalent to clinical validation of stimuli-responsive MSN drug carriers. Key translational questions include predictable degradation and clearance, control of manufacturing-related impurities, reproducible critical quality attributes, clinically relevant trigger intensity, and demonstrated safety and efficacy in appropriate models.

title: Unlocking Intrinsic Chirality in Luminescent Copper Clusters via Intramolecular Spatial Confinement
abstract: Abstract Most luminescent clusters that exhibit pronounced chiral signals typically rely on predesigned chiral ligands; however, stimulating the intrinsic chirality of clusters in the absence of exogenous asymmetric ligands remains a significant challenge. In this study, based on a series of structure-correlated Cu2 clusters, we demonstrate that intramolecular spatial confinement effectively induces distortions in flexible ligands, thereby imparting asymmetry to the cluster framework. This molecular asymmetry further determines the orientation of cluster entities during supramolecular assembly, thus enabling the modulation of chirality across this cluster series between inactive (“off”) and active (“on”) states. In addition, these structure-correlated Cu2 clusters display bright and tunable luminescence, allowing for the fabrication of uniform thin films that function as practical scintillation materials for high-resolution X-ray imaging. Collectively, this work provides a novel perspective for regulating the chiroptical properties of metal clusters through the activation of intramolecular spatial confinement and offers valuable insights into the fabrication of cluster-based nanomaterials with tailored photophysical performances.

title: Covalent Organic Frameworks for Exceptional Removal of PFAS From Water
abstract: ABSTRACT Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants found globally in water, soil, and food, raising widespread public concern because of their high toxicity and the risks they pose to the environment and human health. Although considerable efforts have been devoted over the past decades to developing materials for PFAS removal from water, lowering PFAS to regulation‐compliant concentrations remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report covalent organic frameworks (COFs) engineered through a geometry‐specific strategy for PFAS capture from water. This approach installs peapod‐shaped pairs of closely spaced quaternary ammonium cationic sites, generating cooperative binding pockets that maximize electrostatic interactions with PFAS. The frameworks display ultrafast uptake kinetics, exceptional capture efficiency across ten different PFAS, ultralow equilibrium concentrations, robust regenerability, and cycling stability. Notably, the resulting COF reduces the perfluorooctanoic acid concentration from 1000 to 3.85 ng L −1 in batch systems within 10 min and decrease to as low as 0.82 ng L −1 under flow operations, both surpassing the state‐of‐the‐art materials. These findings establish COFs as a powerful platform for programming pore environments and open an avenue toward unparalleled porous materials for PFAS removal and water treatment.

title: An Experimental MOF-Polymer Latent Space for Composite Design
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have tremendous promise for filtration, catalysis, and sequestration, but they are limited by the polymer matrices in which they must be embedded to form functional composites. Here, we find an experimental approach in which composite performance can be predicted using a single MOF particle. In particular, we attach single MOF particles to atomic force microscope (AFM) probes and find that the forces between the MOF-tipped probe and polymer films can be transformed into an instructive low-dimensional descriptor of MOF-polymer interactions. This two-dimensional latent space provides direct measures of chemical compatibility as well as the work of adhesion and can be used to understand interfacial phenomena in MOF-polymer composites. For example, polymer intercalation is observed via X-ray scattering for MOF-polymer combinations with high chemical-compatibility latent-space variables. Bulk composite performance can also be predicted using the latent space values for cases where the MOF is held constant. For example, a simple linear model was trained to predict CO2 absorption into composites of UiO-66-NH2 based solely on the latent space variables. In addition to providing a rapid way to screen polymer matrices to complement a MOF chosen for its bulk properties, these results suggest that composite performance may be a separable function of bulk properties and the interfacial latent space. In this way, this transfer-learning approach can vastly accelerate the design and understanding of functional composites.

title: Discovery of NIR-II nanocrystals Ag3AuSe2 with near-unity quantum yield
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of second near-infrared (NIR-II) emitting nanocrystals (NCs) with unity photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) is paramount for deep-tissue bioimaging and high-efficiency optoelectronics; however, the PLQY decreases markedly as the emission shifts to longer wavelengths. Herein, we have discovered a novel Ag3AuSe2 (fischesserite) NC system that extends this PLQY-wavelength frontier into the long-wavelength regime, achieving a near-unity absolute PLQY of 98.9% at 1000 nm with a monoexponential decay time of 4.1 µs. The synthesis of the near-single-crystal Ag3AuSe2 NCs hinges on the employment of an Au(I)-octanethiolate coordination polymer, [Au(OTT)]n, as the Au precursor. This precursor enables the regulated release of active gold species and provides a mild redox environment, which are essential for improving crystal quality and suppressing interfacial defects otherwise induced by side reactions. The exceptional brightness of these NCs provides a new paradigm for ultra-high signal-to-noise ratio imaging, fundamentally reshaping the application landscape for NIR-II emitters.

title: Synergistic Dual‐Site Regulation in a Tailored Imine‐COF for Enhanced Hydrogen Peroxide Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) emerge as promising candidates for the photocatalytic production of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). However, precise modulation of the chemical environment of active sites in COFs remains a significant challenge. Based on a molecular engineering strategy, this study focuses on hierarchical regulation of nitrogen coordination environments for efficient photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production through the 2e − ORR. Intrinsic nitrogen configurations (triazine vs. pyridine) are first tailored to construct two types of COFs. The pyridyl‐imine TAPT‐BTPA ( 4 ) optimizes charge carrier separation and extends visible‐light absorption, leading to an enhanced H 2 O 2 production rate of 8.12 mmol g −1 h −1 in aqueous solution containing isopropanol as a sacrificial agent under an O 2 atmosphere. Main‐group metals (In, Sn, and Sb) are then anchored at the pyridine‐imine sites to modulate local electron density further and steer reaction pathways. Structural characterization and activity tests reveal that Sb‐coordinated TAPT‐BTPA‐Sb ( 10 ) induces a unique synergistic effect, redirecting the ORR toward a more favorable stepwise 1e − route. This significant pathway regulation ultimately boosts the H 2 O 2 production rate to 15.3 mmol g −1 h −1 under the same conditions. This work clarifies the decisive role of coordination environment engineering and establishes a molecular‐level design paradigm for advanced H 2 O 2 synthesis photocatalysts.

title: Compression‐Driven Self‐Assembly of Fusion Peptides Into Fibrous Networks Revealed by In Situ Grazing‐Incidence X‐Ray Diffraction
abstract: Fusion peptides (FPs) have emerged as versatile building blocks for nanoscale architectures with potential applications in nanolithography, surface templating, and bioinspired materials. However, most studies of FP self-assembly at fluid interfaces rely on ex situ characterization after transfer to solid substrates, making it difficult to determine whether the observed structures form at the interface or during transfer and drying. Here, we employ grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXD), combined with X-ray reflectivity (XRR), to directly probe in situ the structural evolution of FP monolayers at the air-water interface during uniaxial compression. The results reveal that compression drives the development of lateral molecular order and fibrillar assemblies at the fluid interface. For FP1, increasing surface pressure promotes β-sheet ordering and fibril coherence, with maximum in-plane correlation at an intermediate pressure, whereas further compression partially disrupts this organization. In contrast, FP4 exhibits only short-range order with limited response to compression. These findings identify surface pressure as a physical parameter for controlling peptide organization at fluid interfaces and provide a basis for compression-directed fabrication of tunable peptide nanostructures.

title: Defect-Tolerant Frenkel Exciton Delocalization in Supramolecular Nanotubes
abstract: Abstract Preserving exciton delocalization in the presence of structural and environmental disorder is a central challenge for nanoscale photonic and optoelectronic materials. Here we show that Frenkel excitons in two-dimensional supramolecular nanostructures retain extensive delocalization even in the presence of intentionally incorporated deep-energy traps. Fluorescent trap molecules introduced during the self-assembly of double-walled molecular nanotubes provide a controlled model system in which strong local energetic perturbations are created without significant distortion of the host structure. Increasing the trap concentration shortens the host-exciton PL lifetime from ∼190 ps to ∼15 ps, while polarization-resolved microscopy of individual nanotubes shows that the collective excitonic polarization remains essentially unchanged. Frenkel-exciton calculations based on experimentally established molecular structures reproduce this robustness and reveal that delocalization decreases only weakly because the excitonic wave functions redistribute around the trap sites while remaining extended over large molecular domains. These results demonstrate an intrinsic defect tolerance of delocalized Frenkel excitons in a two-dimensional supramolecular architecture and identify dimensionality as an important design principle for preserving collective excitonic states in structurally imperfect nanomaterials.

title: Synthesis and Structural Characterization of Amine-Functionalized Zinc- and Copper-Based Metal–Organic Frameworks (Zn-BDC-NH2 and Cu-BDC-NH2)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) functionalized with pendant amine groups are of growing interest as tunable, low-cost adsorbent platforms because their pore surfaces can be engineered to interact selectively with polar and ionizable pollutants. In this study, amine-functionalized zinc-based (Zn-BDC-NH2 MOF) and copper-based (Cu-BDC-NH2 MOF) metal–organic frameworks were synthesized from 2-aminoterephthalic acid (BDC-NH2) and the corresponding metal nitrate precursors using a simple, conventional solution-based route in ethanol buffered with sodium acetate at near-neutral pH. The two products were characterized by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). FTIR spectra of both materials showed disappearance of the free carboxylic acid C=O stretch of the parent linker and its replacement by an asymmetric/symmetric carboxylate (COO−) doublet, together with new low-frequency bands assigned to Zn–O and Cu–O stretching, confirming metal–carboxylate coordination, while retained C–N bands confirmed that the –NH2 functionality survived framework assembly in both cases. XRD patterns confirmed the crystallinity of both products, with Cu-BDC-NH2 MOF displaying a greater number of well-resolved reflections extending to higher diffraction angles and a smaller Debye–Scherrer crystallite size (≈51 nm) than Zn-BDC-NH2 MOF (≈80 nm). SEM revealed markedly different morphologies: coarse, angular, plate-like aggregates for Zn-BDC-NH2 MOF versus fine, globular, densely packed nanoparticle clusters for Cu-BDC-NH2 MOF. Together, these results establish a reproducible, low-cost synthetic route to two structurally distinct amine-functionalized MOFs bearing free –NH2 groups, providing a structurally characterized platform for subsequent pollutant-adsorption applications.

title: Electro‐Biocatalytic Dearomative Oxidation–Asymmetric Aldol Cascade Enables Direct Synthesis of Chiral 3‐Hydroxyindolin‐2‐Ones From Indoles
abstract: We present a sustainable electro‐biocatalytic cascade for the highly diastereo‐ and enantioselective synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant 3‐hydroxyindolin‐2‐ones by combining electrochemical dearomative oxidation of indole followed by an abiotic CALB‐catalyzed asymmetric aldol reaction in the same reaction vessel. The versatility of the electro‐biocatalytic cascade was well explored with a wide range of substrates, including indole‐bearing electron‐donating, ‐withdrawing, and halide substituents, along with two representative cyclic ketones, which were successfully transformed into the desired products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 91%) with outstanding stereocontrol, providing up to 99% ee and 99% de . Furthermore, mechanistic investigations, including control experiments and cyclic voltammetry studies, revealed distinct roles for electricity and enzyme catalysis and provided evidence for the involvement of iodinated intermediates in dearomative electrochemical oxidation of indole. The synthetic utility of the cascade protocol was further demonstrated through gram‐scale synthesis. This work establishes a versatile electro‐biocatalytic cascade platform that integrates the sustainability of electrosynthesis with the exceptional selectivity of enzyme catalysis, providing a sustainable and efficient process for the stereoselective synthesis of chiral 3‐hydroxyindoline‐2‐ones.

title: Concentration‐Dependent Self‐Assembly and Nanoparticle Maturation of Reflectins
abstract: ABSTRACT Cephalopods dynamically modulate coloration for camouflage and communication through iridophores whose Bragg reflector‐like ultrastructures contain high‐refractive‐index proteins known as reflectins. However, the mechanisms linking concentration, conformation, and nanoparticle stabilization in full‐length reflectins remain poorly understood. Here, coarse‐grained molecular dynamics simulations of Doryteuthis pealeii reflectin A2 (RfA2) across five concentrations are combined with dynamic light scattering (DLS) and circular dichroism (CD) measurements. The simulations reveal rapid initial protein aggregation followed by slower structural maturation, during which interprotein interaction energy and contact networks continue to evolve. A simulation‐derived concentration‐dependent crossover separates multi‐cluster vs single‐cluster regimes and DLS shows larger assemblies at higher experimental concentrations. The simulations further delineate region‐specific secondary‐structure reorganization and CD demonstrates concentration‐sensitive structural changes with a distinct secondary‐structure redistribution. Moreover, the simulations predict concentration dependence in the contribution of intermolecular contact network reorganization; the L1, L3, and L5 linker regions supplied many of these contacts, with L3 providing the dominant contribution. Overall, these findings establish a molecular‐level framework where concentration governs RfA2 self‐assembly and continued conformational and intermolecular reorganization during maturation, providing insight into sequence‐ and assembly‐level principles regarding iridophore optical function and reflectin‐based materials design.

title: Self-Assembly of Two-Dimensional Open Structures with Adjustable Square Voids
abstract: Abstract Self-assembly of anisotropic particles offers a powerful route to design materials with tailored microstructures. Here we investigate two-dimensional systems of patchy hard rectangles using Monte Carlo simulations and free volume theory, mapping their phase diagram across packing fractions and interaction strengths. Low attraction recovers excluded-volume phase behavior (isotropic–tetratic–smectic), while intermediate attraction strengths feature a broad isotropic–smectic coexistence region. For high interaction strengths our theory predicts, and simulations confirm, a highly ordered “weaver” phase characterized by a four-rectangle unit cell that forms a regular grid of square voids. Although the pure weaver phase forms only in a narrow window of packing fractions, it coexists with either the isotropic gas or smectic solid over a wide range of packing fractions. Patchy rectangles demonstrate how shape together with tunable interactions can be utilized to self-assemble porous materials with precisely adjustable void sizes and geometries and could be realized using DNA origami structures.

title: Advancing CO 2 Electroreduction Toward Multicarbon Products via Catalyst Engineering and Integrated Paired Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction (CO 2 RR) provides a compelling pathway for converting CO 2 into value‐added multicarbon (C 2+ ) products using renewable electricity, yet its technological translation remains limited by coupled challenges spanning catalyst chemistry, reaction microenvironments, reactor architecture, and cathode‐anode integration. This review develops a multiscale framework that connects molecular‐level C‐C coupling with device‐ and process‐level performance. Fundamental CO 2 activation, reaction pathways, electrochemical metrics, and structure–activity relationships are critically examined, with particular emphasis on Cu‐based catalysts and emerging catalyst‐engineering strategies for selective C 2+ synthesis. These catalytic principles are then linked to operando surface states, intermediate coverage, local microenvironments, mass transport, membrane behavior, and electrolyzer configuration under technologically relevant conditions. Beyond cathodic optimization, oxygen evolution and alternative anodic chemistries, including biomass‐derived alcohol oxidation and plastic‐derived stream valorization, are assessed within integrated paired‐electrolysis architectures. Their practical significance is benchmarked through matched current density, full‐cell voltage, carbon and electron efficiency, product concentration, crossover, separation, durability, and realistic feed compatibility. This framework exposes critical catalyst‐reactor‐process trade‐offs and defines design principles for scalable, durable, and economically credible CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ electrosynthesis.

title: Interfacial Confinement Enables Conformal IrOx Nanofilms for Low-Ir-Loading PEM Water Electrolysis
abstract: Abstract Terawatt-scale deployment of proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) requires low iridium (Ir) loading, which disrupts the catalyst layer’s in-plane electronic percolation network and severely degrades performance. Here, we overcome this bottleneck via an interfacial confinement strategy that electrostatically enriches cationic Ir intermediates on the negatively charged, oxygen-deficient TiOx surface, thereby redirecting Ir deposition from three-dimensional island growth to a two-dimensional conformal film on TiO2 supports. The resulting IrOx-NF@TiO2 catalyst with low Ir packing density maintains long-range in-plane electron percolation, reducing reliance on the high Ir loading typically required by conventional IrOx nanoparticle catalysts to establish quasi-continuous conductive pathways. At a loading of 0.166 mgIr cm−2, blade-coated membrane electrode assemblies incorporating this architecture feature ∼7 μm-thick catalyst layers with an Ir packing density of only ∼0.25 gIr cm–3, allowing an ∼84% reduction in Ir use while achieving performance comparable to that of commercial IrO2. This work highlights the potential of supported conformal IrOx catalysts as competitive candidates for next-generation low-Ir PEMWEs.

title: Evolution of Interfacial States Induced by Hydronium–Water Ordering on Au(111)
abstract: Abstract Structured interfacial water can substantially modify charge transfer at solid–liquid interfaces, yet direct spectroscopic evidence for how water ordering reshapes interfacial electronic states remains scarce. Herein, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), we identify parabolic interfacial states (IFSs) arising with the ordered water structures on Au(111), in striking contrast to the insulating nature of disordered water multilayers. Light exposure induces partial dissociation of H2O, and the resulting hydrated protons combine with residual H2O molecules to form ordered Eigen/Zundel-type hexagonal hydronium-water monolayers on Au(111) at 120–140 K. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations based on Eigen/Zundel-type motifs reproduce the experimentally observed IFSs and indicate that the states derive from the renormalized Au(111) Shockley surface state with a reduced effective mass at the water/gold interface. Annealing-driven transition from the Eigen-type to Zundel-type monolayers is evidenced by the distinct changes in the dispersions of the IFSs. These results establish a band-structure perspective for ordered water/metal interfaces and show that hydrated-proton-introduced excess electrons, when confined at a two-dimensional interface, can reshape the interfacial electronic landscape and charge transport.

title: Intrinsically Stretchable Fully π‐Conjugated Polymer Films Enabled by Supramolecular Plasticized Micro‐Crosslinking‐Network for Flexible Polymer Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable fully π‐conjugated polymers (FπCPs) films with a fantastic optoelectronic property and outstanding deformation tolerance capacity, is a promising candidate for the fabrication of flexible optoelectronics devices. However, previous reported stretchable FπCPs films undergo irreversible chain slippage and alignment upon strain release, leading to plastic deformation, and consequently severe performance degradation during cyclic‐deformation operation. Herein, we proposed a supramolecular soft‐micro‐crosslinked strategy to achieve the stretchable p ‐ n FπCPs (P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI) films with a recoverable‐deformation ability for the flexible electronics. Three‐dimensional (3D) supramolecular micro‐crosslinked network formed by oxime‐urethane and hydrogen bonds allow for the excellent elastic deformation to dissipate transient stress while fundamentally suppressing permanent chain slippage. Micro‐crosslinked p ‐ n FπCPs free‐standing films achieved an elongation at break of > 40%. Flexible PLED based on P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI showed a stable green emission with brightness of ∼3300 cd cm −2 . Meanwhile, the performance of transferred PLED based on stretchable micro‐crosslinked films are independent on the tensile ratio (>20%) with a maximum brightness of ∼2000 cd m −2 , revealed the excellent cycle‐deformation‐stability than device based on crosslinked films. Therefore, these supramolecular micro‐crosslinked networks can enhance instantaneous toughness and confer a critical resistance to long‐term stress relaxation and plastic deformation, further ensure the device excellent deformation stability.

title: Multiphase Inorganic-Rich Interphases with Integrated Li-Ion Capture-Transport Ability for High-Rate Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal batteries promise high-energy-density storage but are limited by unstable solid–electrolyte interphases, which couple poor passivation, sluggish Li+ transport, dendritic deposition, and safety risks. Herein, we report a multiphase inorganic-rich solid–electrolyte interphase (m-SEI) containing P- and Al-derived species including Li3P, LiAl5O8, Li3PO4, and Li2Al, which is formed from the in situ reaction between a flame-retardant aluminum diethyl hypophosphite (ADP) interlayer and lithium metal. This multicomponent inorganic SEI enables an integrated capture-transport mechanism by combining high Li+ affinity, facilitated desolvation, and low-barrier Li+ migration pathways in individual inorganic phases and their heterophase interfaces, thereby facilitating rapid Li+ interfacial migration. Its chemical inertness and high Young’s modulus of 17.14 GPa further suppress electrolyte decomposition and Li dendrite growth. As a result, the Li-metal batteries with m-SEI deliver an extended lifespan of 1000 h at a high current density of 4 mA cm–2. Li||NCM811 full cells with a high cathode loading (20 mg cm–2) and ultrathin Li foil (50 μm) retain 80% capacity after 250 cycles, while Li||NCM811 pouch cells retain 90% capacity after 500 cycles. This work establishes the capture-transport mechanism as an effective design principle for regulating Li+ interfacial dynamics and offers a practical interphase-engineering strategy for constructing ion-conductive and chemically protective interphases in durable lithium metal batteries.

title: Beyond acceptor emissivity: interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder regulate nonradiative voltage losses for organic solar cells
abstract: Abstract Suppressing non-radiative energy loss (ΔEnr) is critical for achieving high open-circuit voltage (VOC) in organic solar cells (OSCs), yet it remains unclear whether intrinsic emissive properties of acceptors can reliably predict voltage losses. Here, we report a counterintuitive phenomenon in which a low-emissive acceptor (D6) delivers a significantly reduced ΔEnr compared with the benchmark L8-BO when blended with D18. Despite lower intrinsic emissivity of D6, the D18: D6 system exhibits a markedly higher electroluminescence efficiency and a reduced ΔEnr of 0.153 eV, leading to an enhanced VOC of 0.980 V. Incorporation of D6 into the D18: L8-BO host yields a ternary device with a power conversion efficiency of 21.01%. Sensitive EQE analysis reveals that favorable CT-state energetics partially contribute to the reduced non-radiative loss of D18: D6, while temperature-dependent photoluminescence analysis further identifies suppressed interfacial dynamic disorder as a critical additional factor. While dynamic disorder is significantly increased in the D18: L8-BO blend, it is effectively suppressed in the D18: D6 system, resulting in preserved emissive interfacial states. Complementary structural and kinetic studies demonstrate that D6 modulates aggregation pathways and stabilizes nanoscale morphology, enabling efficient charge transport and reduced recombination. Furthermore, the beneficial role of D6 can be extended to multiple high-performance acceptor systems, demonstrating its general applicability as an interfacial regulator for improving photovoltaic performance. These results highlight that non-radiative voltage loss in OSCs is governed by the interplay between interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder rather than by the intrinsic emissivity of the acceptor alone, providing new insights into the design of low-energy-loss photovoltaic materials.

title: Structural basis of ligand-mediated transition to higher-order rubisco assemblies
abstract: Abstract Proteins often assemble as higher order complexes, underlying a diversity of molecular structures and biological functions. The emergence of protein-protein interactions between binding partners is generally considered to be the primary driver of oligomerization. However, ligand binding has also been demonstrated to affect higher-order assembly, though this phenomenon is not widely considered as a primary driver of oligomerization. Here, we describe the mechanism by which different rubisco oligomeric states are induced via ligand binding. By expanding the phylogenetic sampling of a unique clade of rubisco, we discover a range of oligomeric responses to ligand binding across the phylogeny and identify the structural features responsible for shifts in the oligomeric state that ultimately provide a path to evolving new quaternary structures. Here, we identify a ligand-dependent mechanism giving rise to new protein assemblies, in contrast with the typical process of evolving new protein-protein interfaces directly. Our findings describe a means by which binding and entrenchment of a ligand enables an increase in structural complexity.

title: Mechanisms and Structural Regulation of Metal–Organic Framework Materials for Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction
abstract: Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction can convert CO 2 into high-value chemicals and fuels such as CO, HCOOH, CH 3 OH, and CH 4 by utilizing solar energy, representing an important pathway for carbon resource utilization. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with their tunable metal nodes, organic linkers, and regular pore structures, exhibit unique advantages in CO 2 enrichment, light absorption, charge transport, and stabilization of key intermediates. This review focuses on the mechanisms and structural regulation of MOFs for photocatalytic CO 2 reduction. It first introduces the fundamental processes of photogenerated carrier generation and migration, CO 2 adsorption and activation, proton-coupled electron transfer, and product formation. It then summarizes representative MOF systems based on Zr, Fe, and Ti, as well as the performance characteristics of composites with metal nanoparticles, molecular catalysts, and semiconductors. On this basis, it further analyzes the influence mechanisms of metal-node regulation, linker functionalization, defect engineering, pore-microenvironment modulation, and heterointerface construction on light absorption, charge separation, intermediate adsorption, and product selectivity. Existing studies indicate that the photocatalytic performance of MOFs depends on the synergistic matching of their electronic structure, active sites, and local reaction microenvironment. Future efforts should address challenges including photogenerated charge recombination, structural stability, and selectivity in multi-electron reactions, while combining in situ characterization and theoretical calculations to deepen the understanding of real active sites and reaction pathways, thereby providing a theoretical basis for the rational design of efficient and stable MOF photocatalysts and CO 2 resource utilization.

title: Crystalline NiO:N Templating of Uniformly Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract The buried hole-selective contact in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is expected to transport holes through its bulk while also templating a defect-free self-assembled monolayer (SAM). A crystalline, vacuum-deposited nitrogen-doped NiO (NiO:N) film deterministically templates a uniformly anchored SAM, while the reactive-atmosphere N2/O2 ratio used during pulsed laser deposition (PLD) simultaneously programs bulk hole density and interfacial anchoring chemistry. Nitrogen incorporation is proposed to act as a shallow acceptor that generates Ni3+ states and raises p-type conductivity, whereas the dense, pinhole-free template enforces uniform SAM coverage, fully suppressing the underlying substrate signal and minimizing surface hydroxyl groups relative to discontinuous nanoparticle films. Consequently, NiO:N/SAM-based PSCs achieve a 6.2% relative increase in power conversion efficiency (PCE) over pristine NiO nanoparticles, reaching one of the highest reported performances for vacuum-deposited NiO-based PSCs, with improved thermal and operational stability. These results establish reactive-atmosphere NiO:N as a general, scalable platform for hole-selective contacts in inverted perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Switching of Exciton-Polaritons in Covalent Organic Framework-Based Optical Resonators through Interaction with the Molecular Environment
abstract: Abstract We report a demonstration of a covalent organic framework (COF) integrated into an optical cavity for the realization of exciton–polaritons and their reversible switching through changes in the surrounding molecular environment. Films of COF nanoplates were integrated into Fabry–Pérot resonators engineered to achieve spectral matching between cavity modes and COF excitonic transitions, yielding strong light–matter coupling with a Rabi splitting above 300 meV. The cavity architecture preserves accessibility of the porous framework, enabling interaction with guest molecules. The potential of this interplay is shown by exposing the resonators to water vapor, which induces both a redshift and a pronounced reduction of the COF optical absorption. The observed hypochromic effect drives a reversible shift from strong to weak coupling, effectively switching exciton–polaritons on and off, as guest molecules are desorbed from or adsorbed in the reticular material host. The process is reversible upon desorption, with preservation of structural and optical integrity. These results establish COFs as a versatile platform for chemically tunable polaritonic systems, opening avenues for responsive photonic devices, sensing, and control of light–matter interactions in nanostructured materials.

title: Rational Synthesis of Sulfonic Acid-Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Capture of Trace Strontium in Natural Mineral Water
abstract: Abstract As a typical long-lived radionuclide, strontium-90 (90Sr) possesses persistent radiological hazards and exhibits high migratory and diffusive behaviors in groundwater. However, the development of adsorbents for the efficient and highly selective capture of trace Sr(II) remains a great challenge. In this study, covalent organic frameworks (COFs, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H) with different numbers of sulfonic acid groups were rationally synthesized and applied for capturing Sr(II). The introduction of sulfonic acid groups onto TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H endowed them with high adsorption capacities of 136.4 and 68.3 mg g–1 toward Sr(II), which were 12-fold and 6-fold higher than that of TpPa without sulfonic acid groups, respectively. Meanwhile, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H exhibited fast adsorption kinetics, capturing 99% of Sr(II) within 3 and 10 min, respectively. In addition, TpPa-2SO3H also exhibited high selectivity, excellent anti-interference performance, and regeneration ability without high calcium backgrounds. Characterizations and theoretical calculations demonstrated that sulfonic acid groups in TpPa-2SO3H promoted Sr(II) capture through strong ion-exchange interaction. TpPa-2SO3H was further applied to extract trace Sr(II) in natural Sr-containing mineral water samples. The results showed that the extraction efficiency for Sr(II) exceeded 95% within 5 min. Furthermore, the selectivity for Sr(II) was investigated by the distribution coefficients (Kd), and the Kd was 5.6 × 104 mL g–1 for TpPa-2SO3H toward Sr(II), approximately 400 times higher than those of Na(I) and K(I), respectively. This work not only developed a promising strategy to extract trace Sr(II) from real samples but also broadened the application of COFs in separation science.

title: Reticular Materials as Optical Sensors of Volatile Organic Compounds for Healthcare and Environmental Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are a family of molecules that possess high vapor pressure and are regarded as air pollutants that prevail in both indoor and outdoor settings. Prolonged exposure to VOCs poses a serious risk to human health. On the other hand, VOCs emitted by humans and plants have been recognized as key biomarkers to estimate the status of health and physiology in living beings. Profiling the total content of VOCs in human and plant fluids leads to early diagnosis of diseases and timely treatment. Monitoring the presence of VOCs, either to track air pollution or to estimate the status of health, has therefore commanded increasing attention. Among the various techniques, optical sensing methods have been sought after owing to the considerations of their fast response time, versatility, miniaturization and portability, as well as the possibility of performing non-invasive detection. Advanced functional materials, such as porous reticular solids, including metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), and hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs), are well suited not only as sorbents for the detection and capture of VOCs but also as suitable substrates for various approaches of optical signaling. This review, through recent case studies, presents the advances in the optical sensing of VOCs by reticular materials. In addition, a comparative analysis between various reticular material types has been provided, along with an outline of the current challenges and the opportunities that exist for future research.

title: Guest‐Engineered Intrapore Microenvironments in Resorcinarene‐Based Frameworks for Enhanced Iodine Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient iodine capture by metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) requires the spatial integration of accessible pore space and strong binding sites without compromising framework integrity. Herein, we employ host‐guest encapsulation to functionalize otherwise underutilized pore space of macrocycle‐based MOFs by introducing an organic salt guest, N‐(2‐trimethylammonioethyl)pyridinium dibromide (PyBr) within the cage‐like units of resorcinarene‐based uranium‐organic frameworks (UOF‐1D and UOF‐2D). While maintaining the host framework well, such a modification creates a Br − /N + ‐rich pore microenvironment in as‐synthesized PyBr@UOF‐1D and PyBr@UOF‐2D. The resulting materials exhibit gas‐phase iodine uptakes of up to 3.50 g·g −1 , markedly exceeding those of the pristine frameworks, free guests, and physical mixtures. Spectroscopic analyses and calculations show that confinement enriches iodine around guest sites, where Br − polarizes I 2 and promotes polyiodide/polyhalide formation, while N + electrostatically stabilizes the resulting anions. The enhanced capture originates from improved pore utilization through cooperative confinement and guest‐derived binding interactions. Its successful application to both 1D and 2D UOFs demonstrates the adaptability of guest‐engineered pore microenvironments across distinct architectures, offering a route toward target‐specific separations.

title: Electric-field-assisted interfacial rubrene self-assembly for continuous tuning of liquid crystal pretilt angles
abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates a contact-free, low-temperature strategy for continuously tuning the pretilt angle of nematic liquid crystals (LCs) via electric-field-assisted capillary filling combined with rubrene self-assembly. By applying an AC electric field (0–5 V) across unrubbed, polyimide-free indium tin oxide (ITO) cells during LC injection, the pretilt angle of a rubrene-doped nematic LC mixture can be continuously programmed from approximately 3° (near-planar) to 90° (homeotropic). Contact-angle analysis reveals that increasing the filling voltage dramatically alters the interfacial interaction from a polar-dominated surface to a nonpolar, high-dispersive regime, resulting in a gradual transition from planar to homeotropic LC alignment. Electro-optical and dielectric measurements confirm stable, uniform LC alignment and customized threshold responses across cycles. This field-imprinted interfacial assembly method eliminates mechanical damage and high-temperature thermal processing, offering a scalable route for next-generation flexible, wearable, and tunable photonic devices

title: Hydrometallogel-Templated, Plasmonic Au Nanoparticle Assemblies for NIR-Activated H2 Release from Ammonia-Borane
abstract: Abstract The addition of [Au(acac)(PMe3)] (acac = acetylacetonate) to orotic acid affords the mononuclear complex [Au(N-orotate)(PMe3)] (1) and the dinuclear species [{Au(PMe3)}2(μ-O,N-orotate)] (2), with the crystal structures of two polymorphs of complex 2 fully elucidated by X-ray diffraction studies. Remarkably, complex 1 undergoes ultrasound-induced supramolecular self-assembly in water to form a robust Au(I) hydrometallogel (1-hyd), whereas 2 lacks the capacity to gelate due to coordination-induced suppression of intermolecular hydrogen bonding. The hydrometallogel acts as both a soft template and an in situ gold precursor, enabling the formation of densely packed, belt-like assemblies of plasmonic Au nanoparticles (1-hyd-Au NPs) upon mild and short thermal treatment. These anisotropic nanoarrays display strong interparticle coupling, yielding a broad, red-shifted localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) absorption centered at ca. 650 nm with substantial NIR absorption. Under 808 nm excitation, the system exhibits efficient photothermal conversion accompanied by the generation of localized plasmonic hot spots. Exploiting this dual activation mode, 1-hyd-Au NPs photocatalyse the methanolysis of ammonia-borane, delivering significantly enhanced H2 release relative to purely thermal conditions. The results demonstrate that hydrometallogel-templated Au assemblies provide an effective and modular platform for NIR-driven plasmonic catalysis, integrating supramolecular templating with strong light-matter interactions to boost the dehydrogenation of chemical hydrogen carriers.

title: Skeletal Reconstruction of Tetrazole Rings Enables Synthesis of Fused Triazole–Pyrimidine Bicyclic Energetic Materials
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-rich triazole-fused energetic materials featuring high heats of formation and extended π-conjugation represent crucial candidates for satisfying the dual requirements of high energy and exceptional insensitivity. However, achieving their effortless synthesis remains challenging. Herein, an efficient skeletal reconstruction strategy based on the thermal cleavage of tetrazole was utilized to synthesize a novel [5,6]-fused triazolopyrimidine explosive, TTO-1, and a plausible transformation mechanism was elucidated by theoretical calculations. Subsequent oxidation and self-assembly derivatization afforded a novel low-sensitivity energetic material, TTO-2, alongside a high-energy material, TTO-3. Both TTO-1 and TTO-2 possess favorable insensitivity (IS &gt; 50 J; FS &gt; 360 N) and detonation performance (P = 23.4 and 26.3 GPa, respectively), positioning them as promising candidates for low-sensitivity energetic materials, while TTO-3 displays a highly competitive detonation performance (P = 35.4 GPa). These findings provide valuable insights for the construction of advanced nitrogen-rich fused high-energy materials.

title: Self-assembly versatility of N-acyl amino acids
abstract: N -acyl amino acids (NAAAs) are prebiotically plausible amphiphiles that can emerge from simple fatty acids and amino acids under abiotic conditions. As hybrid molecules combining two fundamental classes of prebiotic building blocks, NAAAs may have contributed to the emergence of structurally and functionally diverse molecular assemblies during early chemical evolution. However, how amino acid side chains influence their self-assembly behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigated the self-assembly of three structurally distinct N -octanoyl amino acids— N -octanoyl-glycine (OA-G-OH), N -octanoyl-L-threonine (OA-T-OH), and N -octanoyl-L-phenylalanine (OA-F-OH)—to evaluate how amino acid side chains affect aggregation propensity and supramolecular structure. Our results indicate that NAAAs differ remarkably in aggregation propensity and generate distinct higher-order structures, potentially conferring functional diversity relevant to prebiotic chemistry and applications in drug delivery, biomedicine, and materials science.

title: Peptide Self‐Assembly: Insights From Functional Short Peptides, Amyloid‐β, and Gluten Peptides
abstract: ABSTRACT In this perspective, we discuss how short peptides can be programmed through sequence design, stereochemistry, terminal modification, and external stimuli to form diverse supramolecular architectures. We then examine how similar molecular principles underlie disease‐associated aggregation, focusing on early Aβ(1–42) assemblies in Alzheimer's disease and proteolysis‐resistant gluten peptide nanostructures in gluten‐related disorders. Attention is given to the detection, stabilization, and modulation of transient oligomeric species, which remain challenging but highly relevant to therapeutic and diagnostic targets. We further highlight how short functional peptides can be engineered to interfere with aggregation pathways in amyloid and nonamyloid aggregopathies, including diabetes‐related amyloids, α‐synuclein, and phenylalanine assemblies. Together, these examples illustrate the cross‐applicability of concepts from supramolecular materials chemistry to molecular pathology. This perspective emphasizes that understanding peptide self‐assembly at the molecular level is key to both exploiting and controlling its biological consequences.

title: Negative Gauge Factor Piezoresistance in Soft Strain and Pressure Sensors: Mechanisms, Materials, and Emerging Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Soft strain and pressure sensors underpin wearable electronics, soft robotics, and human‐centered healthcare, yet most piezoresistive devices rely on a positive gauge factor (pGF), in which resistance increases as deformation disrupts conductive pathways and continuous power is needed to register an event. Negative‐gauge‐factor (nGF) materials, whose resistance decreases under deformation, offer a fundamentally different route. Importantly, a negative gauge factor does not by itself imply low power: continuously conducting nGF devices still require an applied bias and constant monitoring, whereas near‐zero‐standby‐power, event‐triggered operation is enabled specifically by switch‐type nGF devices that are insulating at rest and turn on only under strain. This review classifies reported nGF systems into four mechanistic categories: intrinsic nGF from strain‐induced band‐structure modulation (Si, MoS 2 , PtSe 2 /PdSe 2 , SiC); composite nGF that transfers this response into polymer matrices and textiles; polymer‐reorganization nGF in conducting polymers; and architecture‐induced nGF engineered through tunneling barriers, contact closure, and compliant geometries. We discuss how these mechanisms enable low‐power switch‐type sensors, wearable health and motion monitoring, electronic skins, and smart textiles, and outline the challenges to establishing nGF piezoresistance as a design principle for energy‐efficient soft electronics.

title: Gradient‐Integrated High‐Strength and High‐Toughness Cellulose Triboelectric Materials for Enhanced Charge Storage and Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid advancement of wearable electronics places ever‐increasing demands on the electrical and mechanical properties of materials. Cellulose offers renewability, low cost, and high durability for green wearables, but its weak electron‐donating ability and poor charge‐transport efficiency limit triboelectric performance. Interfacial mismatch between the electrode and triboelectric layers also induces charge dissipation, further aggravating this problem. Inspired by the Janus structure found in sea urchin spines, a gradient‐integrated triboelectric material (MWCNT/T‐CNFs) was fabricated via vacuum‐assisted layer‐by‐layer filtration. The resulting gradient electric field forms a highly compatible interface between the triboelectric layer and the electrode layer, providing a low‐impedance path that effectively suppresses charge dissipation. Consequently, the material achieves a surface charge density of 20.5 nC cm −2 (931.8% that of pure T‐CNFs) and excellent cycling stability (8044 cycles). The integrated interface offers strong adhesion, far outperforming conventional electrode tapes, while the gradient design alleviates stress concentration, yielding a tensile strength of 126.33 MPa and toughness of 9.11 MJ m −3 (535.9% that of pure T‐CNFs). The material also exhibits good water stability and high‐temperature resistance. This study addresses the key limitations of low surface charge density and interfacial mismatch in cellulose materials, providing a solid foundation for interface design in wearable electronics.

title: Shear-induced structure and rheology of multichain amphiphilic diblock and triblock copolymers in dilute solutions
abstract: This study presents a computational investigation of self-assembly and rheological behavior of multichain amphiphilic block copolymers under varying chain length (N), architecture, composition (f), and shear rate (γ˙). Using Brownian dynamics simulations, we systematically examined bead-spring model multichain diblock and triblock copolymers with N = 12–48 beads, f ranging from 0 to 1.0, and γ˙ spanning 0–0.1 ns−1. These systems self-assemble into spherical, prolate, rodlike, and oblate/disk micelles, with transitions governed by each variable, where increasing shear rate drives nonmonotonic prolate-to-rod redistribution, aggregating at weak shear rate before fragmenting at high rates; longer chains strengthen the dominant rod population; and higher hydrophobic fraction shifts assemblies from rod toward sphere at f = 1. Triblock copolymers form bridged assemblies, where hydrophobic end-blocks anchor into distinct micellar cores while hydrophilic middle blocks span the intervening space, producing solution viscosities up to half an order of magnitude greater than counterpart diblock systems. Linear viscoelastic spectra show terminal power-law scaling (G′ ∼ ω2, G″ ∼ ω1) with a liquidlike response (G″ > G′) throughout the accessed window. The triblock relaxation is governed by chain-end escape. The bridge fraction rises with the chain length as a longer midblock spans neighboring cores but falls with hydrophobic fraction as the shorter midblock forces chains into loops. The bridge lifetime saturates with increasing chain length once bridging is established (N ≥ 24), while the loop lifetime shortens with chain length yet increases with hydrophobic fraction, providing qualitative design insights relevant to flow-responsive polymer self-assembling systems.

title: Research Progress on Biodegradable Porous Metallic Bone Implants
abstract: Abstract The clinical efficacy of traditional inert metallic bone implants is limited by stress shielding caused by mechanical mismatch and by the need for a second operation to remove the implant. Biodegradable metals have become a focus of research in bone repair materials because they degrade and are absorbed in vivo, their mechanical properties can be tuned, and their biocompatibility is favorable. The introduction of a porous structure further modulates the apparent elastic modulus of the material to match the host bone tissue and provides a suitable microenvironment for cell adhesion, proliferation, and osseointegration. This review summarizes the characteristics and the current status of research on the three major biodegradable metal groups, namely, the Fe-, Mg-, and Zn-based systems. It compares the advantages and limitations of fabricating porous metallic scaffolds by electrodeposition, sintering, space-holder casting, and additive manufacturing. A mechanistic framework is proposed that links alloy composition, pore architecture, degradation kinetics, and the time-dependent evolution of mechanical properties, in which the weakening caused by matrix dissolution competes with the strengthening caused by the deposition of corrosion and mineralization products. The mechanical compatibility window defined by matching the mechanical degradation rate of the scaffold to the rate of bone regeneration is then analyzed, and a dimensionless ratio of the two rate constants is proposed as a criterion for this matching. Finally, future directions in this field are discussed, with the aim of providing a reference for the development of high-performance biodegradable porous metallic bone implants.
